mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A (Hague Apostille Convention member destination): notarize the Korean-origin document before a Korean notary public; then obtain a single Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs; deliver the apostilled document to the destination. Stop there; do not add consular legalization. Parallel Path B (non-member destination): notarize before a Korean notary public; authenticate at the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs; legalize at the embassy/consulate of the destination country located in the Republic of Korea; if the destination country's internal rules require a final authentication by its Ministry of Foreign Affairs, that occurs after arrival. Never chain Path A and Path B.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All counterparties, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and named bank signatories must be screened against the Consolidated United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, HM Treasury sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Korea's unilateral designations under the Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction Act. PEP screening must cover foreign and domestic PEPs, their family members, and close associates using a risk-based approach required by FATF Recommendation 12 and KoFIU reporting guidance. Any exact or fuzzy match must trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and, where required, a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU within the statutory deadline; no incorporation may proceed on a positive match without written compliance clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registration Information Center (IROS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Commercial Act Articles 555-557 and Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules, the official trade name must be registered in Hangul. The registry applies a four-tier naming screen: (1) identical name in the same jurisdiction is rejected; (2) a name with identical pronunciation or Korean transliteration in the same industry is rejected; (3) a name so similar that it may confuse the public with an existing enterprise in neighboring business lines is rejected; (4) any foreign-language word must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul, and the English operative name is permitted only as a supporting notation, never as the controlling registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Supreme Court registration official, the applicant may, within 14 days, file an immediate objection with the competent district court under the Commercial Registration Rules and the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act. The objection must state the legal basis for registrability of the proposed name and append the rejected receipt, proposed articles of incorporation, and registry search evidence. After court adjudication, if the name remains unavailable, the applicant should revise the trade name using a structurally different Korean transliteration and resubmit to the same registration office; there is no official extension of the 30-day name reservation, so a fresh search and reservation are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office/commercial mailbox is rejected as a registered office for this industry when it is a mere mail-drop address; Korean Commercial Registration Rules require a real, fixed place of business, and the National Tax Service may strip the tax registration if no substantive premises are identified. Banks under Financial Action Task Force-aligned onboarding rules will treat a virtual office as high-risk and may decline to open the operational account or approve Retainer_Wire and Wise_B2B payrails. A virtual suite with dedicated meeting room, actual lease, visible signage, and access to company records can be maintained if full documentary evidence is filed with the registry and tax office; however, for licensed executive search and headhunting, the Ministry of Employment and Labor will expect on-site supervision of placement records and PIPA-compliant personal data processing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection may be triggered by tax office site visits for new registrants, employment agency licensing reviews, bank account opening premises checks, and local authority business closure inspections. Checklist: display of registered signboard, availability of paid employees, original lease contract, corporate seal and books, employment placement license for headhunting activities, payroll and tax invoice records, privacy notices. Quantified risk: 20-25% annual probability for executive search firms operating from virtual offices; under 5% for genuine leased office premises with full staffing and signage.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), particularly Articles 289, 290, 295, 297, 317, 329 and 363; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 5 and 6, as applicable for a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa; Enforcement Decrees thereunder; Employment Security Act for operational licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Division); online filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (ireg.go.kr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Corporation (beop-in seollip deunggi sincheongseo) accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation (jeonggwan).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa. All subscribed shares must be issued and fully paid before incorporation registration; the share subscription price is deposited into a temporary incorporation bank account and cannot be withdrawn until registration. No blocked escrow account, no reserve deposit, and no administrative capital threshold is required for ISIC 7830 executive search and headhunting services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA (STOCK COMPANY), REPUBLIC OF KOREA

Date: [DATE]
Registered Office: [ADDRESS], Seoul, Republic of Korea

Pursuant to Article 368(4) of the Commercial Act and Article [●] of the Articles of Incorporation, the Board of Directors of the corporation, duly constituted and acting unanimously upon the consent of all incumbent directors, hereby adopts the following formal resolutions at the first board meeting held for the organization of the corporation after incorporation.

FIRST: SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT. The Board acknowledges and confirms the incorporation subscription of [●] issued ordinary shares having par value of KRW [●] each, representing total stated capital of KRW [●] and total paid-in capital of KRW [●]. The Board confirms that each incorporator has fully paid the subscription price in cash to the temporary incorporation deposit account opened at [●] Bank under the name of the corporation, and that the bank has issued a certificate of payment of the subscription price. No subscription price has been offset by any claim against the corporation, no unlawful contribution in kind was accepted for the initial incorporation, and all legal pre-incorporation expenses and obligations are admitted and ratified.

SECOND: BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes and instructs the Representative Director to open and maintain corporate current accounts, foreign exchange accounts, savings accounts and payment processing facilities with licensed financial institutions in the Republic of Korea. The board expressly authorizes such financial institutions to honor payment orders, accept deposits, process wire transfers, encash checks, execute electronic funds transfers and settle all fees on behalf of the corporation. Financial institutions may conclusively rely on the sole signature of the Representative Director, or on the joint signatures of any two persons designated by the Representative Director, and may receive, obtain receipt for, and discharge all money and negotiable instruments.

THIRD: REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts [ADDRESS] as the registered office of the corporation within the Republic of Korea, being the venue for service of process and statutory notices. The Board authorizes the Representative Director to bargain, execute, amend and terminate leases, subleases and related facility agreements necessary for the registered office and for the ordinary operation of the executive search and headhunting business.

FOURTH: STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints [NAME] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] as Director, and [NAME] as Auditor, if required, to serve until the first ordinary general meeting of shareholders and until successors are appointed or re-elected. Each appointee consents to office and confirms no legal disqualification under the Commercial Act or Employment Security Act. The Representative Director is conferred with full authority to execute, deliver, file and prosecute all corporate documents, tax registrations, bank instructions, labor office registration for paid employment placement services, and any other instrument necessary for the corporation’s lawful activities.

FIFTH: CORPORATE SEAL. The Board adopts the corporate seal (beop-in-in-gam) of the corporation and authorizes its registration with the court, tax office and financial institutions. The seal shall be kept in the custody of the Representative Director with a duplicate custodian designated by the board.

SIXTH: POST-INCORPORATION AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes and directs the Representative Director to file the application for corporation registration with the competent district court, obtain the Certificate of Corporation Registration, file business registration with the National Tax Service, register with the Ministry of Employment and Labor for the paid employment placement business under the Employment Security Act, open corporate bank accounts, and take all further acts necessary to commence lawful operation.

This resolution is effective as of the date first written above and shall be recorded in the corporate minutes book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (ireg.go.kr) and a licensed Korean notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-filing name search through the Internet Registration Office to confirm that the proposed company name is not deceptively identical to an already registered entity. Draft and approve Articles of Incorporation in Korean official execution copy, specifying the corporate purpose as executive search and specialist technology headhunting (ISIC 7830 / NAICS 561312), the number and par value of authorized ordinary shares, the registered office address, the method of publication, and the number of directors and auditor. Ensure all incorporators execute the articles in person or through validly appointed attorney-in-fact, and notarize the Articles before a court-licensed notary public. Prepare the corporate seal engraving and the seal registration data.
required_dossiers: Company name availability search receipt
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original execution copy)
Valid government-issued identity documents of all incorporators
Power of attorney for proxy incorporators, if applicable
Corporate seal specimen and seal engraving order form
Consent to appointment of directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name conflicts with an existing registration, choose a distinctive alternative, rerun the search and amend the articles. If the notary raises conformity issues, revise the objects and statutory clauses to align with the Commercial Act and the Employment Security Act, re-execute the articles and obtain a new notarization; the SLA clock restarts upon resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Temporary Incorporation Deposit Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation deposit account in the name of the proposed corporation at a commercial bank in Korea. The bank will assign a provisional corporate designation because the entity is not yet registered. Each incorporator must deposit the full amount subscribed for ordinary shares from a personal account by wire transfer or cash deposit. Deposits may not be made by way of setoff against any claim, and subscription payments must be made in full before incorporation registration. Upon completed deposit, require the bank to issue a certificate of payment of the subscription price, which must name the corporation and state the amount held. For a foreign investor, complete the foreign exchange reporting through a licensed foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and retain the inward remittance certificate.
required_dossiers: Temporary incorporation account opening application
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (certified copy)
Identity and residence records of each incorporator
Subscription price bank remittance slips
Foreign exchange inward remittance report (if foreign investor)
Instruction letter designating account signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the capital deposit certificate because of identity mismatch, correct the account title or supplemental declaratory documents and re-submit the certificate request. If a foreign exchange reporting error is notified, file a post-report with the foreign exchange bank and obtain confirmation, then resubmit to the incorporation bank; timely correction is available within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division, District Court of the Republic of Korea for the registered office; online portal: ireg.go.kr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Corporation to the registration division with competent jurisdiction over the registered office no later than two weeks after full payment of the subscription price. The application must attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank certificate of payment of subscription price, written consent of each director and auditor, lease or title evidence of the registered office, representative identity records, corporate seal registration application, and payment of court fees and registration tax. The registration officer examines statutory conformity with the Commercial Act and, upon approval, enters the corporation in the commercial register, issuing the Certificate of Corporation Registration and the corporate seal register. Legal personality vests on the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Corporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original)
Bank certificate of payment of subscription price
Written acceptance of office by each director and auditor
Corporate seal registration application and seal specimen
Lease agreement for the registered office
Court fee and registration tax payment receipts
Identity documents of directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplemental instruction or reason for correction, file the missing documents or a correction declaration within the period stated, usually two weeks. If the application was routed to the wrong registration office, file a withdrawal and re-file in the correct district court. For urgent matters, submit a written request for expedited review and deliver any curative filings in person to the registration window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Corporate Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office; online via Hometax (home.tax.go.kr); commercial bank for corporate account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Corporation Registration, file a business registration (sa-eop-ja deungrok) application with the competent district tax office using Hometax or by visiting the tax office. Select the Korean Standard Industrial Classification code corresponding to employment placement and executive search. Provide the corporation registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, registered office lease agreement and representative identity document. After the tax office issues the Business Registration Certificate, open a corporate current account at a commercial bank in the corporation’s name using the corporate certificate, seal certificate, lease agreement and representative identity. Register the corporation for e-tax invoices and VAT compliance, and keep all filing proof in the corporate books.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporation Registration
Corporate seal certificate
Business registration application form
Registered office lease agreement and deposit receipt
Representative Director's identity card or passport
Articles of Incorporation (copy)
Proof of corporate bank account opening (if already opened)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business classification, amend the application with the correct KSIC code and a supporting corporate purpose clause. If lease records are challenged, produce a certified lease contract and bank transfer evidence of the security deposit. If the application is suspended, resubmit through Hometax with a correction note and obtain an expedited reassessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid Employment Placement Business Registration under the Employment Security Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Employment and Labor Office of the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL) having authority over the principal office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing fee-charging executive search and headhunting activities, apply for registration as a paid employment placement agency with the competent Regional Employment and Labor Office. Submit the prescribed application form under Articles 19 and 20 of the Employment Security Act, together with a business plan describing the placement model, the fee schedule, the office plan demonstrating interview space, the names and criminal record certificates of the representative and responsible staff, and confirmation that no disqualifying offense exists. Attach the Business Registration Certificate, Certificate of Corporation Registration, corporate seal certificate, articles of incorporation and lease evidence. Once reviewed and approved, the MOEL issues a paid employment placement business registration certificate. Display a certified fee schedule, maintain placement records, and submit statutory reports during inspections.
required_dossiers: Paid employment placement business registration application
Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Corporation Registration
Corporate seal certificate
Certificate of no disqualifying criminal record for the representative and staff
Office lease agreement and floor plan
Fee schedule and executive placement service rules
Articles of Incorporation and director list
Identity and family relation records as requested by MOEL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended for incomplete documents, file the missing dossiers at the same Regional Employment and Labor Office within the administrative cure period. If denied, submit a written reconsideration to the Minister of Employment and Labor or file an administrative appeal with the Central Administrative Appeals Commission within 90 days, and simultaneously correct any procedural defects set out in the denial notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for manufacturing or physical industrial licensing; the statutory labor-market licensing authority is the Ministry of Employment and Labor, Regional Employment and Labor Office, which supervises paid employment placement services for ISIC 7830 executive search and headhunting. No factory, chemical, assembly, or warehousing authority applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Paid Employment Placement Business Registration (유료직업소개사업 등록) under Articles 19 and 20 of the Employment Security Act. This is the statutory operating license required before advertising or invoicing fee-based C-suite executive search and specialist tech headhunting placements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable: the Ministry of Environment is the nominal EIA agency for physical facilities, but an executive search office creates no construction, manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing project subject to the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA tier applies. ISIC 7830 (NAICS 561312) is a pure consulting and data-match service with no effluent discharge, no process emissions, no physical land alteration and no hazardous material handling. Environmental Registration is likewise not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, combustion stack, cooling water, chemical storage, or hazardous waste stream arises from executive search and headhunting operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for high-risk Civil Defense fire permits because the scope is pure office-based executive search. Standard office occupancy compliance under the Building Act and Occupational Safety and Health Act applies, including basic fire extinguisher placement, evacuation signage, electrical safety, sanitary facilities and building use approval from the local fire station. No special industrial fire safety certificate, chemical license, or hazardous materials clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); export-related customs and clearance: Korea Customs Service (KCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A Chusik Hoesa incorporated in Korea is a domestic Korean legal person and, where foreign-owned, remains subject to standard Korean entity registration with the National Tax Service. Step 2: File the business registration application with the competent district tax office through HomeTax within 20 days of commencement of business; the application includes the foreign-corporation domestic place of business registration where the Chusik Hoesa is itself a foreign corporation with a Korean establishment. Step 3: Submit corporate constitutive documents, certificate of incorporation, foreign corporate registry extract (if foreign entity), proof of Korean registered office, bank account details, and power of attorney appointing a local tax representative if the company has no Korean management presence. Step 4: NTS validates the application and issues a 10-digit Business Registration Certificate that simultaneously functions as the Corporate Tax TIN, Value-Added Tax VAT ID, and withholding account identification; no separate entity-level identifier is issued. Step 5: The same registration completes VAT registration because the Chusik Hoesa is a Korean domestic taxable person. Step 6: Use the TIN/VAT ID on all electronic tax invoices, customs declarations, foreign exchange settlement reports, and statutory VAT and corporate income tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists for a Chusik Hoesa; it is mandatorily classified as a resident entity-level taxpayer, with the consolidated corporate tax payment election available only to qualifying wholly-owned Korean groups.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No mandatory turnover threshold for a corporation; VAT registration is triggered by the commencement of any Korean taxable business activity. An individual sole proprietor with annual turnover at or below KRW 80,000,000 may qualify as a simplified taxable person, but that threshold does not apply to a Chusik Hoesa, which must register from the first taxable supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for VAT-registered corporations. Each taxable supply of executive-search services must be evidenced by an e-tax invoice issued through HomeTax or an NTS-recognised service provider, transmitted to NTS on or around the time of supply, and retained in the central NTS electronic tax invoice system. The invoice must state the supplier and recipient TIN/VAT IDs, supply date, supply value, VAT amount or zero-rated export classification, and a description of the service. NTS performs central cross-matching of e-tax invoice issuances and acceptances to detect fraudulent invoice chains. No physical fiscal stamping or continuous-control device is required in this industry.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, zero-rating applies to exports of goods and prescribed services supplied to non-residents for use or consumption outside Korea. For C-suite executive search and headhunting services, the Korean Chusik Hoesa may charge 0% VAT when the client is a non-resident legal person, the engagement letter and fee invoice are denominated in foreign currency, the actual search deliverable and advice are provided to and used by the foreign client outside Korea, and payment is received in foreign exchange. Zero-rating is denied if the service is for a Korean employer, for a Korean branch of a foreign company, or where the foreign-client arrangement lacks substance. Input VAT attributable to the zero-rated export supply is creditable and refundable via the normal VAT return mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: No Korean Customs export declaration is raised for a pure service export; the mandatory zero-rating substantiation bundle consists of (a) a signed foreign-currency engagement letter or search mandate from the non-resident client; (b) the electronic tax invoice issued as a zero-rated export supply; (c) a Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Korean bank evidencing receipt of the fee in foreign currency from the actual overseas client; (d) service-delivery records such as candidate shortlists, interview logs, placement confirmations, and progress reports proving the deliverable was supplied to the non-resident client; and (e) a reconcilable export register mapping each invoice to the corresponding remittance and VAT return entry.

If incidental tangible goods, such as printed assessment materials or market-research binders, are physically exported in connection with an executive-search engagement, the exporter must additionally retain the Korea Customs Service export declaration, an export bill of lading or air waybill, and shipment receipt to prove removal from Korea.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audits zero-rated export claims by matching e-tax invoices, VAT returns, export registers, and bank foreign-exchange settlement data. If the export evidence file is incomplete, the foreign client is found to be linked or sham, or the service is recharacterised as domestic, NTS may retroactively assess 10% VAT, claw back any refund paid, add interest, and impose under-declaration penalty tax (10% of the unpaid VAT for ordinary failure and

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and subordinate Foreign Exchange Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized but tightly regulated foreign exchange system. The Korean won is fully convertible on the current account for bona fide trade and service transactions, including executive search retainers and cross-border professional fees, subject to documentary substantiation and reporting through designated foreign exchange banks. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, borrowing, loans, and inbound equity subscriptions, are generally free but require advance notification, post-transaction reporting, or a certificate of acquisition if structured as a foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Profit and dividend remittance is permitted once corporate tax has been settled, but the paying bank will typically require audited financial statements, a board resolution, tax payment certificates, and a Foreign Exchange Bank confirmation. Repatriation of capital upon liquidation or share disposal requires a further validation of the original inbound currency declaration. No mandatory surrender of export proceeds exists today, meaning the corporate may retain foreign currency in authorized foreign currency accounts, but all settlements must pass through licensed Korean banks. Non-resident shareholders face practical hurdles: they must appoint a domestic agent or ensure the bank's e-banking systems can authenticate their identity, and they must submit source-of-funds and tax-residency evidence. The overall assessment is that the regime is business-friendly but form intensive, and a foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa must maintain meticulous records of every cross-border wire, FX deferral, and corporate action to avoid penalty and delayed profit repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters in South Korea are generally required to receive export proceeds within 180 days from the date of export clearance, unless an extension or exception is approved in advance by the designated foreign exchange bank. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the entity may retain up to 100% of export proceeds in a foreign currency account. However, the receipt must be reported to the pursuing bank, and any failure to collect within the statutory window must be justified with documentation such as insolvency certificates, dispute evidence, or settlement delay schedules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD multicurrency) with Linked Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Corporate Operating Current Account with Foreign Currency Settlement Module
Multi-Currency Corporate Checking Account and Trade Services Escrow Account
Cross-Border Business Account with Dedicated FX Deal Desk Interface

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise B2B have a very low direct onboarding viability in South Korea. Foreign electronic money institutions and payment service providers are not authorised to independently service domestic corporations unless they obtain an e-money or payment institution licence from the FSC or enter into a compliant local partnership with a licensed Korean bank or registered money transmitter. Most global EMIs lack such licences, so the Chusik Hoesa should not rely on them as a primary treasury rail. A Wise B2B account could be considered only as a downstream sub-router for low-value secondary disbursements, and only if the funds first pass through a licensed domestic bank-based corporate account and clear all Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting obligations. The legally sound path is to use traditional SWIFT wires through Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, or Hana with proper purpose codes, and to treat any EMI as a non-bank auxiliary rather than a regulated settlement channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa, the statutory representative director is generally required to appear physically at the Korean bank branch for account opening under Article 3-2 of the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and bank-specific AML procedure standards. Remote opening for foreign directors is not a blanket right; however, most tier-1 banks permit remote application with a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, passport, foreign corporate registration certificate, and a video interview conducted by the bank's compliance officer. Even with remote acceptance, the bank normally imposes a tailored two-week initial restriction on cross-border transactions and may require the physical presence of the registered director within 90 days for the bank's KYC renewal cycle. In practice, the most frictionless method is for the Korean resident tax representative or a locally appointed corporate secretary to accompany the foreign director for a one-day in-branch procedure, after which full digital treasury channels can be activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership structure appears indirect or opaque, particularly where the headhunting agency is owned by a holding entity outside Korea
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete ownership chain chart, certified Korean corporate registry extracts, foreign company certificates of good standing, a Beneficial Ownership Declaration Form, and notarised passports of all natural persons holding 10% or more, together with apostilles or consular legalisation where required

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and economic substance mismatch because the entity's revenue is expected from retainer wires and the initial share capital is low
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Verified source-of-funds letters for initial capital, bank reference letters from existing foreign banking relationships, audited financial statements or a detailed business plan with cash-flow projections, an organisational chart showing headhunting staff, lease contracts for physical office space, and evidence of ongoing corporate expenses and payroll

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty or jurisdiction exposure if the headhunting agency has clients or subcontractors in sanction-sensitive or high-risk territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanction screening certifications, CDD files for every maintainer and large-ticket client, a written AML compliance policy, transaction monitoring procedures, hit-adverse media remediation, and copies of client contracts that include anti-money laundering warranties and the underlying search-mandate purpose

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anomalous expected transaction profile with frequent splitting of retainer payments or use of third-party payment methods
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A fully executed retainer framework agreement, project acceptance certificates, per-mandate placement records, detailed invoices matching each headhunting deliverable, proof that retainer wires originate from the contracting employer's own bank account, and a formal KYC file on each corporate client with ultimate beneficial owner identification

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection for a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa should be structured as a formal foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if the foreign shareholder subscribes new shares. The investor must first file a Foreign Investment Notification with MOEF through a designated Korean exchange bank, open a temporary Foreign Currency Capital Account at that bank, remit the capital via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own bank account, and then submit a Foreign Capital Verification Certificate to the court and the national tax service after issuance of shares. For non-equity loans or simple working-capital funding, the entity must file a Foreign Borrowing Report with BOK through the exchange bank, maintain an interest-rate and maturity schedule, and route the funds through a domestic bank using the appropriate balance-of-payments purpose code. All inbound wires must state clearly in the remittance remarks the purpose code, such as 'FDI Equity Investment' or 'Foreign Loan', and the Chusik Hoesa must retain the bank-dispatched certificate and customs declaration for future profit remittance and liquidation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and service disbursements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 messages from the Chusik Hoesa's main KRW/USD account at a licensed Korean bank. For cross-border headhunting fees, the preferred rail is a direct MT103 to the beneficiary bank with purpose code 'Executive Search Services' or 'Management Consulting Fees' and supporting retainer or placement invoicing. For trade settlements involving contractual engagements, commercial letters of credit are admissible but generally over-engineered for services; documentary collections are suitable when the client requires proof of performance before releasing payment. The entity should never use unstructured omnibus clearing through third-party EMIs as the primary rail because the reporting chain becomes fragmented. Domestic withdrawals and remuneration to foreign consultants can be made via MT103 or via insured local wires within KRW if the consultant holds a Korean account. All disbursements must be logged against the underlying contract, in order to present a coherent audit trail to both the bank and the Financial Intelligence Unit during periodic AML transaction-pattern reviews.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD spot and plain-vanilla forward contracts with licensed domestic foreign exchange banks to hedge firm retainer receivables denominated in USD

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) entered into offshore strictly through supervised financial institutions and permitted only for eligible corporates with an underlying real-risk exposure; NDFs cannot be used for speculative positions by non-financial companies

Cross-currency swaps between KRW and USD, or KRW and other major currencies, limited to matching real asset, liability, or cash-flow exposures and requiring hedge-letter documentation acceptable to the regulating bank and BOK
Option collars and vanilla currency options when offered by a licensed Korean dealer, but only as a risk-mitigation overlay on a documented forecast of cross-border retainer fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return for the prior fiscal year, including statement of financial position, statement of profit or loss, and tax reconciliation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end where the fiscal year is December 31, i.e., within 3 months of the fiscal year-end; a corporate income tax extension of up to 4 months may be requested, but extension does not stay interest or surtax accrual.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax; underreporting carries an additional tax of 10% (or 30% for false, malicious, or deliberately concealed returns); unpaid tax accrues daily interest at 0.022% from the original due date; sustained non-filing can lead to tax seizure, business license closure, administrative dismissal of the corporate registration, and criminal referral for attempted tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax return (local income tax surcharge on corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through the Webrate local tax system or designated local tax e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year-end; for companies with a non-calendar fiscal year-end, by the last day of the 3rd month after the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled local income tax returns incur a late-filing surtax of 20% of the unpaid local income tax; delayed payment accrues daily late-payment interest at 0.022%; chronic delinquency causes coercive collection, refusal of local-tax clearance certificates, suspension of government contracts, and possible public auction of corporate assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly Value-Added Tax returns (preliminary and final periods) for services, executive-search fees, retainers, and business expenses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25th day of the month following each calendar-quarter period: Q1 (Jan-Mar) by April 25; Q2 (Apr-Jun) by July 25; Q3 (Jul-Sep) by October 25; Q4 (Oct-Dec) by January 25.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT underreporting or late filing attracts statutory surtax of 10% of the unpaid VAT (20% for no-filing or intentional concealment), plus daily interest at 0.022%; continued failure may result in tax investigation, immediate collection, business suspension, and criminal penalties under the VAT Act and Tax Offense Punishment Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Private employment placement and executive-search annual operation and placement performance report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Regional Employment and Labor Office of the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the end of the fiscal year, or within 90 days of the fiscal year-end for a non-calendar fiscal year; actual MOEL enforcement rules may require the report within the same statutory window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing false placement data can trigger administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Employment Security Act, suspension of the private employment placement license for up to 3 months, or revocation of the statutory headhunting license; responsible directors may also face separate administrative sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory audit report and audited financial statements (only when the Korean external-audit thresholds are exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), with electronic delivery via DART e-disclosure for public-interest companies; for listed entities, also to the Korea Exchange
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the auditor's report must be available for presentation at the annual ordinary general shareholders' meeting, which must be held no later than March 31; the FSS/DART filing for companies subject to the external-audit requirement is due within 2 weeks after the date the audit report is delivered to the company, and in any event before the end of the statutory AGM window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a certified auditor, refusal of the auditor's access, or failure to file the audit report with the FSS subjects responsible directors and officers to criminal fines and imprisonment under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; fines can reach KRW 30,000,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years; the FSS may also issue corrective orders and suspend administrative benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convening of the annual ordinary general shareholders' meeting, approval of the annual financial statements, appointment/re-appointment of directors and statutory auditor, and maintenance of meeting minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No direct filing to a corporate registry in Korea; the statutory record is maintained at the registered office and must be produced to shareholders, auditors, or the court on demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual ordinary general shareholders' meeting must be held within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the meeting must be convened by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting or to lay the financial statements before shareholders violates the Korean Commercial Act; directors may be subject to statutory fines of up to KRW 5,000,000, civil liability for unlawful acts, and injunctive or derivative shareholder litigation; persistent non-compliance can induce a court order for dissolution of the Chusik Hoesa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership report and non-resident share transfer report (event-driven; no separate annual renewal for a non-public low-risk headhunting corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) through a designated reporting channel; non-resident share transfers are reported to the designated foreign-exchange bank or KOTRA for foreign direct investment records; the register of members is maintained at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial beneficial owner report within 30 days after incorporation; updated report within 30 days after any change in controlling beneficial ownership, share transfer, pledge, trust holding, or change of UBO details; non-resident share transfer report also due within 30 days of the transaction calendar date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a beneficial-ownership report under the Korean Beneficial Owner Information Act attracts enforcement fines up to KRW 20,000,000, with higher criminal exposure for knowingly false reports; failure to report non-resident share transfers under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act can lead to administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000, seizure of the transfer proceeds, and possible invalidation of the foreign payment/title transfer.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa is legally required to engage an independent Korean certified public accountant as statutory external auditor if, at the close of the immediately preceding fiscal year: (a) balance-sheet total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 8,900,000); (b) balance-sheet total assets equal or exceed KRW 7,000,000,000 (approx. USD 5,200,000) and the average full-time headcount is at least 100 employees; or (c) the company is a public-interest entity, a listed stock company, a financial company, or a company specifically designated by the Financial Services Commission. There is no standalone turnover/revenue threshold in the Korean external-audit statute; sales volume is relevant only in the FSC's discretionary designation. An executive-search and headhunting Chusik Hoesa with assets below KRW 7,000,000,000 or with assets between KRW 7,000,000,000 and KRW 12,000,000,000 and headcount below 100 employees is generally audit-exempt unless designated.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korea Adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed companies and public-interest entities; non-listed audit-exempt companies may prepare statutory financial statements using K-GAAP / SME accounting standards, but where external audit applies, the audit opinion must state conformity with Korean accounting standards, and the books must be kept in Korean won with Korean-language financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Act on Reporting and Using Information on Beneficial Owners of Corporations, the initial beneficial-ownership report must be filed with the Financial Services Commission within 30 days after incorporation. Thereafter, a change report is required within 30 days of any transfer of shares or membership interests that changes a controlling beneficial owner, any pledge or trust arrangement affecting beneficial ownership, or any update to the name, address, or shareholding percentage of an existing UBO. For transfers involving a non-resident purchaser or seller, the company must also file a foreign-exchange transaction report with a designated foreign-exchange bank or KOTRA within 30 days of the transfer and must contemporaneously update the register of members. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation return for a non-public, low-risk executive-search corporation; annual compliance is satisfied by keeping the UBO schedule current, recording transfers in the register of members, and retaining proof of the 30-day filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges over Shares and Charges
Minutes of Board of Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 360 - 720 per year for a commercial registered-office address, service-of-process, and corporate-secretarial agent in Seoul; if the company maintains its own office, this cost is not applicable.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 18,000 per year for a small or mid-sized Chusik Hoesa if the external-audit thresholds are exceeded; USD 0 for audit-exempt companies.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% (maximum Korean corporate tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion; lower statutory rates of 9% and 19% apply up to KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion respectively)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays in Free Economic Zones, investment tax credits, R&D expense tax credits, and special tax support for innovative ventures; no patent box is currently granted, but technology acquisition deductions and foreign tax credits materially lower effective tax rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Standard Tax Base and Tax Return (Form 25) and accompanying schedules; mandatory e-filing through NTS HomeTax portal at www.hometax.go.kr by the taxpayer or a licensed tax agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, plus a semi-annual interim tax return for corporations with prior-year corporate tax exceeding KRW 1 billion.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the closing date of the fiscal year, automatically extended to four months on application; calendar-year corporations must file on or before March 31 (May 31 with extension). The interim tax return is due within two months after the first six months of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification and registration details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Chusik Hoesa corporate registration number and foreign shareholder nationalities; attach a power of attorney and TRC of any non-resident director/shareholder if the company is managed partly abroad to avoid permanent establishment misclassification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year period, reporting entity type, and tax classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate calendar year period; note whether the entity is a domestic corporation or a foreign corporation with a Korean branch; if non-resident executive search services are rendered from overseas, do not include such revenue unless a Korean permanent establishment exists, but strict factual substance documentation is required to override Korean-source income rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from executive search fees, retainers, project-based placement commissions, and reimbursed costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue derived from headhunting mandates, including non-resident clients, with separate schedules for cross-border candidate sourcing and invoices in foreign currency converted at the Bank of Korea exchange rate; unreported foreign-currency retainer income triggers TP adjustments and criminal tax evasion examination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses, salaries, marketing, database subscriptions, background-check costs, and professional fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a detailed foreign payment ledger showing contracts, invoice numbers, and supporting evidence of services actually performed. If payments are made to foreign related parties, include WHT certification and proof of DTA beneficial ownership; expenses paid to tax-haven shell vendors are not deductible and trigger penalty tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustment from book income to taxable income, including transfer pricing, nondeductible entertainment, and bad debts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter positive or negative adjustments required by TP documentation; include arm’s length benchmarking of headhunting margins and management fees. Non-resident subcontracted search fees must be benchmarked against Korea-comparable search agencies; failure produces automatic income adjustments and a 40% negligence surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, prepayments, foreign tax credits, and non-resident DTA relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax credits for R&D in recruitment technology, SME investment credit, and foreign income taxes paid on Korean-sourced royalties. Non-resident beneficial owners receiving dividends or royalties must cite the applicable DTA article and attach TRC and beneficial ownership declaration to obtain reduced WHT or credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable, including interim return prepayments and late-paid tax interest
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply graduated rates to each bracket, subtract interim tax prepayment and withheld taxes, and compute balance due with NTS payment voucher. If the DTA reduced rate is disputed, pay under protest at the statutory rate and file a refund claim with the district tax office to avoid expiration of the refund period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and false return surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes: 10% for an inadequate return, 20% for an unfaithful return, 30% for concealment, and 40% for intentional aggravated concealment; daily late-payment interest at 0.022%; criminal referral for intentional fraud can add imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to twice the evaded tax; personal assets of controlling directors can be attached after a non-payment blacklist review.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% corporate income tax withheld on dividends plus 2% local income tax surcharge (aggregate 22%) when paid to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority and dated no earlier than the year of payment, (ii) provide a beneficial ownership statement confirming that it owns the shares and derives the income for its own account and is not an agent or conduit, and (iii) file a request for reduced withholding or refund with the Korean district tax office having jurisdiction over the payer. The payer must obtain these documents before remittance; if not, the payer must withhold at 22%, and the beneficiary must file a refund claim within the statutory limitation period with DTA-required interpretation evidence and economic substance proof.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest and royalties to non-residents is 20% plus local surcharge of 2% totaling 22%; most Korean DTAs reduce dividends to 5-10% when 10% or more capital is held, interest to 10-15%, and royalties to 5-10%, subject to OECD-compliant beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion; any prior-year related-party cross-border transaction amount exceeding this threshold requires Local File and Master File; a Country-by-Country Report is separately required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies the general anti-abuse rule and substance-over-form principle in the Framework Act on National Taxes. Although no separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation exists, the Korean tax court scrutinizes whether the executive search agency has real people, premises, decision-making powers, and contracts in Korea; core income-generating activities of sourcing, interviewing, negotiating, and billing candidates must be substantiated in Korea. A paper company that merely passes invoices through a zero-tax jurisdiction will have its dividends and royalties recharacterized, lose treaty benefits, and be subject to CFC income imputation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Fabricated Headhunting Invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Chusik Hoesa intentionally issues or receives inflated, fictitious invoices for non-existent C-suite candidate search, market mapping, or background verification from a related foreign shell entity, thereby reducing taxable profits and retaining undisclosed cash abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: intentional concealment of income attracts a false-return surcharge of 40% of unpaid tax, daily overdue interest 0.022%, and criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to twice the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign fraudulent invoices are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and surcharges; the NTS may pierce the corporate veil and attach personal real estate and bank accounts, impose an overseas travel ban after blacklisting, and recommend criminal indictment leading to imprisonment. Civil restitution to the tax office follows if corporate assets are insufficient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Non-Resident Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean headhunting agency pays dividends, management fees, royalty costs, or subcontract fees to a non-resident vendor or shareholder using a payment rail such as Wire or Wise B2B without applying the 22% withholding or a certified DTA reduced rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, non-collection or late remittance of withholding tax attracts an aggregate surcharge of 10% to 50% of the withheld amount, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022% and compulsory collection of the omitted withholding tax from the payer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director is obligated as a withholding agent; personal assets are subject to attachment, and the director is placed on the high-value delinquent taxpayer disclosure list. Intentional failure exposes the director to criminal liability and possible travel bans under the National Tax Collection Act; a foreign director may be blacklisted and face restriction of visa and business capacity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: DTA Treaty Shopping through Shell Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident shareholder or intermediary incorporated in a tax-favored jurisdiction with no office, personnel, or decision-making operators invoices Korean executive search fees and then causes the Chusik Hoesa to reduce dividend or royalty withholding under a DTA while the ultimate beneficial owner remains undisclosed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The general anti-abuse rule recharacterizes the transaction and denies treaty benefits; additional income tax equal to the reduced WHT or benefits saved is assessed with a 40% unfair understatement surcharge; supporting documents submitted contrary to fact invoke criminal false-document penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will lift the corporate veil when the entity is a mere sham; directors of the Korean company are personally liable up to the amount of taxes avoided, and the beneficial owner-director is subject to tax penalty plus criminal imprisonment. The NTS issues a tax payment demand and blacklist or travel ban until full restitution is made.
